'''Yuri Tsolakovich Oganessian'''{{efn|{{langx|ru|Юрий Цолакович Оганесян}}, {{IPA|ru|ˈjʉrʲɪj tsɐˈlakəvʲɪtɕ ɐɡənʲɪˈsʲan|IPA}}; {{langx|hy|Յուրի Ցոլակի Հովհաննիսյան|Yuri Ts'olaki Hovhannisyan}}, {{IPA|hy|juˈɾi tsʰɔlɑˈki hɔvhɑnnisˈjɑn|IPA}}.<ref name="sci.am"/><ref name="president.am"/> Oganessian is the Russified version of the Armenian last name [[Hovhannisyan]]. The article on Oganessian in the ''[[Armenian Soviet Encyclopedia]]'' (1980) described him as an "Armenian Soviet physicist".<ref>{{cite book|title=Armenian Soviet Encyclopedia Volume 6|date=1980|location=Yerevan|publisher=Armenian Encyclopedia Publishing House|page=[[:s:hy:Էջ:Հայկական_Սովետական_Հանրագիտարան_(Soviet_Armenian_Encyclopedia)_6.djvu/572|572]]|language=hy|quote=ՀՈՎՀԱՆՆԻՍՅԱՆ Յուրի Ցոլակի (ծն. 14.4.1933, Դոնի Ռոստով), հայ սովետական ֆիզիկոս|title-link=Armenian Soviet Encyclopedia}}</ref>}} (born 14 April 1933) is a Russian and Armenian [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] who is best known as a researcher of [[superheavy element]]s.<ref name="Chapman" /> He has led the discovery of multiple [[chemical element]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/28416|website=CERN Courier|date=2 April 2001|title=EPS introduces new Lise Meitner prize|publisher=IOP Publishing |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715121023/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/28416 |archive-date=15 July 2007}}</ref><ref name="jinr.ru" /> He succeeded [[Georgy Flyorov]] as director of the Flyorov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions at the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] in 1989 and is now its scientific director.<ref name="flerovlab" /> The heaviest known element, [[oganesson]], is named after him, only the second time that an element was named after a living person, and the only one who is still alive (the other is [[seaborgium]], named for [[Glenn T. Seaborg]], who died in 1999).<ref name="Chapman"/>{{efn|The names [[einsteinium]] and [[fermium]] for elements 99 and 100 were proposed when their namesakes ([[Albert Einstein]] and [[Enrico Fermi]]) were still alive, but were not made official until Einstein and Fermi had died.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hoffman |first1=D. C. |author-link1=Darleane C. Hoffman |last2=Ghiorso |first2=A. |author-link2=Albert Ghiorso |last3=Seaborg |first3=G. T. |title=The Transuranium People: The Inside Story |year=2000 |publisher=[[World Scientific]] |isbn=978-1-78-326244-1 |pages=187–189}}</ref>}}

==Personal life==
Yuri Tsolakovich Oganessian was born in [[Rostov-on-Don]], Russian SFSR, USSR on 14 April 1933<ref name="isaran"/> to [[Armenians in Russia|Armenian]] parents.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Shevchenko|first1=Nikolay|title=Moscovium joins the periodic table|url=https://www.rbth.com/science_and_tech/2016/06/10/moscovium-joins-the-periodic-table_601921|work=[[Russia Beyond the Headlines]]|date=10 June 2016|quote=...Yuri Oganessian, a Russian nuclear physicist of Armenian heritage... |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303025209/https://www.rbth.com/science_and_tech/2016/06/10/moscovium-joins-the-periodic-table_601921 |archive-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=New element discovered by Armenian scientist included in Periodic Table|url=https://armenpress.am/eng/news/869997/new-element-discovered-by-armenian-scientist-included-in-periodic-table.html|agency=[[Armenpress]]|date=30 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220230829/https://armenpress.am/eng/news/869997/new-element-discovered-by-armenian-scientist-included-in-periodic-table.html |archive-date=20 December 2018}}</ref> His father, Tsolak, was from [[Iğdır|Igdir]] (now in Turkey),<ref name="Ashxarhi Hayer"/> while his mother was from [[Armavir, Russia|Armavir]] in what is now Russia's [[Krasnodar Krai]].<ref name="noev-kovcheg"/> Oganessian spent his childhood in [[Yerevan]], the capital of [[Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic|Soviet Armenia]], where his family relocated in 1939. His father, a [[Thermal engineering|thermal engineer]], was invited to work on the [[synthetic rubber]] plant in Yerevan. After the [[Eastern Front (World War II)|Eastern Front]] of [[World War II]] commenced, his family decided to not return to Rostov since it was occupied by Germans. Yuri attended and finished school in Yerevan.<ref name="noev-kovcheg"/><ref name="sci.am"/><ref name="Ashxarhi Hayer"/> He initially wanted to become a painter.<ref name="Ashxarhi Hayer"/>

Oganessian was married to Irina Levonovna (1932–2010), a violinist and a music teacher in [[Dubna]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Оганесян Ирина Левоновна |url=http://dubna.org/p/?id=19691 |website=dubna.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116094034/http://dubna.org/p/?id=19691 |archive-date=16 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Памяти Ирины Оганесян |url=http://www.dubnapress.ru/culture/384-2010-12-08-12-50-16 |website=dubnapress.ru |language=ru |date=8 December 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220230903/http://www.dubnapress.ru/culture/384-2010-12-08-12-50-16 |archive-date=20 December 2018}}</ref> with whom he had two daughters.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Yakutenko|first1=Irina|title=Бацилла творчества|url=https://lenta.ru/articles/2010/04/26/oganesian/|work=[[lenta.ru]]|date=26 April 2010|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Titova|first1=Anna|title=Легенда № 118 [Legend #118]|url=http://expert.ru/russian_reporter/2017/08/legenda-h-118/|website=expert.ru|publisher=Expert Online|language=ru|date=2017}}</ref> As of 2017, his daughters resided in the U.S.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gray |first1=Richard |title=Mr Element 118: The only living person on the periodic table |journal=[[New Scientist]] |date=11 April 2017 |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg23431210-600-up-and-atom-breaking-the-periodic-table/}}</ref>

Oganessian speaks Russian, [[Armenian language|Armenian]],<ref name="Ashxarhi Hayer"/> and English.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mileham |first1=Rebecca |title=Cold war, hot science |journal=Research Culture: Collaboration Collections |date=October 2018 |page=44 |url=https://royalsociety.org/-/media/policy/projects/changing-expectations/The-Collaboration-Collection.pdf?la=en-GB&hash=DF1DCC34F61D73DAC639F9CDC86B9D9B |publisher=[[The Royal Society]] |quote=...says Oganessian, in excellent English. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220225161101/https://royalsociety.org/-/media/policy/projects/changing-expectations/The-Collaboration-Collection.pdf?la=en-GB&hash=DF1DCC34F61D73DAC639F9CDC86B9D9B |archive-date=25 February 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Poliakoff |first1=Martyn |author1-link=Martyn Poliakoff |title=The Element Creator - Periodic Table of Videos |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1VaY9N7Alq0 |website=[[Periodic Videos]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220319195206/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1VaY9N7Alq0 |archive-date=19 March 2022 |date=12 April 2017 |access-date=8 May 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==
{{quote box
| width = 30%
| align = right
| quote = "A remarkable physicist and experimentalist… his work is characterised by originality, an ability to approach a problem from an unexpected side, and to achieve an ultimate result."
| source = Flyorov on Oganessian, 1990<ref name="Chapman"/>
}}

Oganessian graduated from the [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] (MEPhI) in 1956.<ref name="jinr.ru"/><ref name="isaran"/> He thereafter sought to join the [[Kurchatov Institute|Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy]] in Moscow, but as there were no vacancies left in [[Gersh Budker]]'s team, he was instead recruited by [[Georgy Flyorov]] and began working at the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] (JINR) in [[Dubna]], near Moscow.<ref name="Chapman"/><ref name="isaran"/>

Oganessian became director of the Flyorov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions at JINR in 1989, after Flyorov retired, and had the job until 1996, when he was named the scientific director of the Flyorov laboratory.<ref name="flerovlab"/>

===Discovery of superheavy chemical elements===
During the 1970s, Oganessian invented the "cold fusion" method, a technique to produce transactinide elements ([[Superheavy element|superheavy elements]]).<ref name="Chapman"/> Though they share a name, this process is unrelated to the unproven energy-producing process also named [[cold fusion]]. Oganessian's process was crucial for the discoveries of elements from 106 to 113.<ref name="Chapman"/> From the mid-1970s to the mid-1990s, the partnership of JINR, directed by Oganessian, and the [[GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research]] in Germany resulted in the discovery of six chemical elements (107 to 112): [[bohrium]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Oganessian|first1=Yu.Ts.|last2=Demin|first2=A.G.|last3=Danilov|first3=N.A.|last4=Flerov|first4=G.N.|last5=Ivanov|first5=M.P.|last6=Iljinov|first6=A.S.|last7=Kolesnikov|first7=N.N.|last8=Markov|first8=B.N.|last9=Plotko|first9=V.M.|last10=Tretyakova|first10=S.P.|title=On spontaneous fission of neutron-deficient isotopes of elements 103, 105 and 107|journal=Nuclear Physics A|volume=273|issue=2|year=1976|pages=505–522|doi=10.1016/0375-9474(76)90607-2|bibcode=1976NuPhA.273..505O }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Münzenberg|first1=G.|last2=Hofmann|first2=S.|last3=Heßberger|first3=F. P.|last4=Reisdorf|first4=W.|last5=Schmidt|first5=K. H. |last6=Schneider|first6=J. H. R.|last7=Armbruster|first7=P.|last8=Sahm|first8=C. C.|last9=Thuma|first9=B.|s2cid=118312056|year=1981|title=Identification of element 107 by α correlation chains|journal=Zeitschrift für Physik A|volume=300|issue=1|pages=107–8|doi=10.1007/BF01412623|bibcode = 1981ZPhyA.300..107M|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238901044}}</ref><ref name="isaran"/> [[meitnerium]], [[hassium]],<ref>{{cite report|first1=Yu. Ts. |last1=Oganessian |first2=G. M. |last2=Ter-Akopian |first3=A. A. |last3=Pleve |display-authors=etal |year=1978 |title=Опыты по синтезу 108 элемента в реакции <sup>226</sup>Ra + <sup>48</sup>Ca |trans-title=Experiments on the synthesis of element 108 in the <sup>226</sup>Ra+<sup>48</sup>Ca reaction |language=ru |publisher=[[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] |url=http://www.iaea.org/inis/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/13/643/13643968.pdf |access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> [[darmstadtium]], [[roentgenium]], and [[copernicium]].<ref name="Chapman"/>

His newer technique, termed "hot fusion" (also unrelated to [[nuclear fusion]] as an energy process), helped lead to the discovery of elements 113 to 118, completing the [[period 7 element|seventh row]] of the [[periodic table]].<ref name="Chapman"/> The technique involved bombarding [[calcium]] into targets containing heavier radioactive elements that are rich in neutrons at a [[cyclotron]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Glanz |first1=James |author-link1=James Glanz |title=Scientists Discover Heavy New Element|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/07/science/07element.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=6 April 2010}}</ref> The elements discovered using this method are [[nihonium]] (2003; also discovered by [[Riken]] in Japan using cold fusion),<ref name=04Mo01>{{cite journal|title=Experiment on the Synthesis of Element 113 in the Reaction <sup>209</sup>Bi(<sup>70</sup>Zn,n)<sup>278</sup>113|year=2004|journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan|volume=73|issue=10|pages=2593–2596|doi=10.1143/JPSJ.73.2593|bibcode=2004JPSJ...73.2593M|last1=Morita|first1=Kosuke|last2=Morimoto|first2=Kouji|last3=Kaji|first3=Daiya|last4=Akiyama|first4=Takahiro|last5=Goto|first5=Sin-ichi|last6=Haba|first6=Hiromitsu|first7=Eiji |last7=Ideguchi|first8=Rituparna |last8=Kanungo|first9=Kenji |last9=Katori|first10=Hiroyuki |last10=Koura|first11=Hisaaki |last11=Kudo|first12=Tetsuya |last12=Ohnishi|first13=Akira |last13=Ozawa|first14=Toshimi |last14=Suda|first15=Keisuke |last15=Sueki|first16=HuShan |last16=Xu|first17=Takayuki |last17=Yamaguchi|first18=Akira |last18=Yoneda|first19=Atsushi |last19=Yoshida|first20=YuLiang |last20=Zhao|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[flerovium]] (1999),<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Oganessian | first1 = Yu. ==Recognition==
{{stack|[[File:Yuri Oganessian 2017 stamp of Armenia.jpg|thumb|Oganessian on a 2017 Armenian stamp]]}}
[[Sherry Yennello]] has called him the "grandfather of superheavy elements".<ref name="Chapman"/> Oganessian is the author of three discoveries, a monograph, 11 inventions, and more than 300 scientific papers.<ref name="jinr.ru"/>

Oganessian has been considered worthy of a [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|Nobel laureate in Chemistry]],<ref>{{cite news |title="Заслуживают "Нобеля" Юрий Оганесян, Артем Оганов и Валерий Фокин" |url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/2825336 |work=[[Kommersant]] |date=5 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210825181918/https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/2825336 |archive-date=25 August 2021 |language=ru |quote=«Заслужил своего "нобеля" Юрий Оганесян из Объединенного института ядерных исследований.}}</ref> including by [[Alexander Sergeev (physicist)|Alexander Sergeev]], former head of the Russian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Medvedev |first1=Yuri |title=Перевернуть пирамиду |url=https://rg.ru/2018/12/18/prezident-ran-rasskazal-kak-povysit-nashi-shansy-na-nobelia.html |work=[[Rossiyskaya Gazeta]] |issue=285 |date=18 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811131746/https://rg.ru/2018/12/18/prezident-ran-rasskazal-kak-povysit-nashi-shansy-na-nobelia.html |archive-date=11 August 2020 |language=ru|quote= Александр Михайлович, и все же ваш прогноз. Кто из наших ученых может в ближайшее время получить заветного Нобеля? Многие очевидным претендентом считают академика Юрия Оганесяна... <br /> Александр Сергеев: Конечно, кандидатура достойнейшая. Очень надеюсь, что ему поможет наступающий год, который Генеральная ассамблея ООН объявила Годом Периодической таблицы химических элементов.}}</ref>

===Oganesson===
{{Main|Oganesson}}
During early 2016, science writers and bloggers speculated that one of the superheavy elements would be named oganessium or oganesson.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cantrill |first1=Stuart |title=New kids on the p-block |journal=[[Nature Chemistry]] |date=26 January 2016 |url=http://blogs.nature.com/thescepticalchymist/2016/01/new-kids-on-the-p-block.html |archive-date=9 August 2020 |access-date=20 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809004948/http://blogs.nature.com/thescepticalchymist/2016/01/new-kids-on-the-p-block.html }}</ref> The [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] (IUPAC) announced in November 2016 that element 118 would be named [[oganesson]] to honor Oganessian.<ref>{{cite web |date= 2016-11-28|url=https://iupac.org/what-we-do/periodic-table-of-elements/|title=Periodic Table of Elements|publisher=[[IUPAC]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://iupac.org/iupac-announces-the-names-of-the-elements-113-115-117-and-118/|title=IUAPC announces the names of the elements 113-115-117-118|date=2016-11-30|publisher=[[IUPAC]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Names proposed for new chemical elements |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-36485631 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |date=8 June 2016}}</ref> It was first observed in 2002 at JINR, by a joint team of Russian and American scientists. Directed by Oganessian, the team included American scientists of the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]], California.<ref name="pp2002">{{cite journal|author=Oganessian, Yu. T.|display-authors=etal|title=Results from the first {{chem|249|Cf}}+{{chem|48|Ca}} experiment|url=http://www.jinr.ru/publish/Preprints/2002/287(D7-2002-287)e.pdf|journal=JINR Communication|location=JINR, Dubna|date=2002}}</ref> Prior to this announcement, a dozen elements had been [[List of chemical elements named after people|named after people]],{{efn|12 other elements named in honor of people: [[curium]], [[einsteinium]], [[fermium]], [[mendelevium]], [[nobelium]], [[lawrencium]], [[rutherfordium]], [[seaborgium]], [[bohrium]], [[meitnerium]], [[roentgenium]], [[copernicium]]; in addition, the intention behind the name [[flerovium]] was to honour Flerov.}} but of those, only [[seaborgium]] was likewise named while its namesake ([[Glenn T. Seaborg]]) was alive.<ref name="Chapman"/> (The names [[einsteinium]] and [[fermium]] were suggested when their namesakes, respectively [[Albert Einstein]] and [[Enrico Fermi]], were still alive; however, by the time the names became official, Einstein and Fermi had both died.) As Seaborg died in 1999, Oganessian is the only currently living namesake of an element.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Van Noorden |first1=Richard |s2cid=211729809 |title=Four new element names proposed for periodic table |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |date=8 June 2016 |doi=10.1038/nature.2016.20069 |url=https://www.nature.com/news/four-new-element-names-proposed-for-periodic-table-1.20069|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=St. Fleur |first1=Nicholas |title=Four Elements on the Periodic Table Get New Names |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/09/science/four-elements-on-the-periodic-table-get-new-names.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=8 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Feltman |first1=Rachel |title=For the second time in history, a living scientist has an element named in his honor |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/speaking-of-science/wp/2016/06/09/for-the-second-time-in-history-a-living-scientist-has-an-element-named-in-his-honor/?noredirect=on |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |date=9 June 2016}}</ref>

===Honors and awards===
In 1990, Oganessian was elected Corresponding Member of the Soviet Academy of Sciences and in 2003 a Full Member (Academician) of the Russian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="isaran"/>

Oganessian has [[honorary degree]]s from [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] (2002),<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary doctorates of the faculties of natural sciences|url=https://www.uni-frankfurt.de/63113600/Honorary-doctorates|website=uni-frankfurt.de}}</ref> [[University of Messina]] (2009),<ref>{{cite web|title=International Conference: Nuclear Reactions on Nucelos and Nuclei|url=http://newcleo.unime.it/conf2009/Third_circular_conference_2009.pdf|website=unime.it|date=5-9 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170619084852/http://newcleo.unime.it/conf2009/Third_circular_conference_2009.pdf|archive-date=19 June 2017|quote=In honour of Yuri Oganessian for his laurea honoris causa that will be conferred by the University of Messina.}}</ref> and [[Yerevan State University]] (2022).<ref name="YSU2022"/> In 2019, he was elected as an Honorary Fellow of [[St Catharine's College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Yuri Oganessian|url=https://www.caths.cam.ac.uk/directory/professor-yuri-oganessian|website=caths.cam.ac.uk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807122411/https://www.caths.cam.ac.uk/directory/professor-yuri-oganessian |archive-date=7 August 2020}}</ref>

====Recognition in Armenia====
Oganessian was granted Armenian citizenship in July 2018 by Premier [[Nikol Pashinyan]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Նիկոլ Փաշինյանը Յուրի Օգանեսովին ՀՀ քաղաքացիություն է շնորհել |url=http://yerkirmedia.am/social/yuri-oganesov-pashinyanqaxaqaciutyun/ |agency=[[Yerkir Media]] |date=10 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712065631/http://yerkirmedia.am/social/yuri-oganesov-pashinyanqaxaqaciutyun/ |archive-date=12 July 2018 |language=hy}}</ref> Oganessian is a member of the Board of Trustees of the Foundation for Armenian Science and Technology (FAST). He is also the chairman of the international scientific board of the [[Yerevan Physics Institute|Alikhanian National Science Laboratory]] (Yerevan Physics Institute).<ref>{{cite news |title=President Sargsyan receives renowned scientists Yuri Oganessian and Ani Aprahamian |url=https://armenpress.am/eng/news/911469/president-sargsyan-receives-renowned-scientists-yuri-oganessian-and-ani-aprahamian.html |agency=[[Armenpress]] |date=6 November 2017}}</ref> In 2017, [[HayPost]] issued a postage stamp dedicated to Oganessian.<ref>{{cite web |title=Yuri Oganessian |url=https://www.haypost.am/en/1514466350 |website=haypost.am|date=28 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220230634/https://www.haypost.am/en/1514466350 |archive-date=20 December 2018}}</ref> The [[Central Bank of Armenia]] issued a silver [[commemorative coin]] dedicated to Oganessian and the element oganesson (Og) in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Collector coins have been put into circulation |url=https://www.cba.am/EN/News/Pages/news_12-09-19_1.aspx#sthash.p9F7hOid.dpbs |website=cba.am |publisher=[[Central Bank of Armenia]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220415181909/https://www.cba.am/EN/News/Pages/news_12-09-19_1.aspx%23sthash.p9F7hOid.mE8poZa8.dpbs |archive-date=15 April 2022 |date=14 April 2022}}</ref> He was also named honorary professor of [[Yerevan State University]] in April that year.<ref name="YSU2022">{{cite web |title=Յուրի Հովհաննիսյանին շնորհվեց ԵՊՀ պատվավոր պրոֆեսորի կոչում [Yuri Hovhannisyan was awarded the title of YSU Honorary Professor] |url=http://www.ysu.am/news/hy/honorary-professor |website=ysu.am |publisher=[[Yerevan State University]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418134808/http://www.ysu.am/news/hy/honorary-professor |date=15 April 2022|archive-date=18 April 2022 |language=hy}}</ref>
